newsitem.title: UK: Centrica beats grey market forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Centrica beats grey market forecasts.

text.p: The performance of shares in Centrica Plc exceeded analysts' expectations on their first day of grey market trading on Monday, while those of the larger BG Plc closed pretty much in line with forecasts.
Shares in the two companies, which are due to emerge formally from the chrysalis of British Gas Plc on Wednesday, are expected to start trading fully later this week.
Shares in BG PLc, which will incorporoate British Gas's international gas, oil and gas exploration businesses, and its gas pipeline and storage company Transco, closed at 172-1/2 pence on Monday.
Analysts said this was close to consensus forecasts for a price of around 175 pence and would value the group at nearly 7.6 billion stg.

However Centrica shares were being quoted at 70 1/2 pence per share, towards the top end of a broad market range of between 40 and 82 pence per share. This would give the domestically-oriented group a market valuation of almost 3.1 billion stg.

Centrica will inherit the troubled gas supply and trading businesses of British Gas, as well as the Morecambe Bay gas field. Analysts said its shares had benefited from signs that inroads into British Gas's domestic customer base in the counties of Avon and Dorset, which became the second region to enjoy full supply competition on Monday, could be limited.

Williams de Broe analyst Peter Hollobone said Centrica may also have profited from a rethink of the value of the Morecambe Bay assets, and from a perception that Centrica could eventually be spilt into regional companies that might be taken over.
Centrica has already said it wanted to be able to price gas on a regional basis in order to deal with competition more flexibly.

BG meanwhile was also boosted on Monday by a report that French state-owned utility Gaz de France could buy as much as three billion cubic metres a year of British gas via a new interconnector between the east coast of England and Zeebrugge in Belgium.
"This means the end is in sight for the problem of take-or-pay contracts," Hollobone said.
Shares in British Gas closed up 1 pence at 244 1/2.
